records.name: Connecticut
records.current_summary:
Connecticut is listed in a July 2026 national legal-risk map among the federation's Most Protective states — those that have "gone above and beyond" in safeguarding transgender people's rights — and equality-map research (data as of September 2026) counts Connecticut among the states whose healthcare "shield" laws protect trans people, their families and providers, including people travelling from states where care is banned, against out-of-state civil or criminal action.

Federal 2025 document and passport restrictions still apply to visitors here as in every state.

sources.claim: July 2026 national legal-risk ranking built from a rubric over thousands of tracked anti-trans bills (youth-care bans, bathroom bans, birth-certificate/driver-license restrictions, end of legal recognition): Connecticut sits in the fifteen-state 'Most Protective' tier (CA, CO, CT, HI, IL, MA, MD, MN, NJ, NM, NY, OR, RI, VT, WA), whose laws have 'gone above and beyond in safeguarding' trans rights. Contrast tier: worst-law states carry up to 5-year prison terms (Idaho) or arrest policy for gender-identity bathroom use (Florida).

MAP Transgender Healthcare Equality Map (data as of 27 Sep 2026) lists Connecticut as 'State has shield law or executive order 2022': the shield/refuge law protects patients and providers from civil or criminal charges when care legal here was banned in the home state — directly relevant to visitors travelling from ban states. National picture on the page: 16 states + D.C. (38% of trans population 13+) hold shields; 32 states + 5 territories (56%) hold none; youth-care bans tracked, some permanently blocked.

records.name: Massachusetts
records.current_summary:
An independent July 2026 legal-risk map places Massachusetts in its most-protective group — states offering refuge to people fleeing restrictive jurisdictions — and national equality-map research records this state's shield and non-discrimination provisions as covering gender identity and enforceable against out-of-state actions arising from other states' restrictions (per the research dossier's read of the interactive map).

Federal 2025 document and passport restrictions still apply here as across the federation.
records.current_localsOnly: The state's only recorded departures from peer protective states are health-insurance coverage details - resident-facing, and invisible to a visitor.
